verdict.rationale: Working Copy's own docs say a private key can be generated inside the app and attached to an Identity. They also say keys can live on the Secure Enclave, the app clones over ssh, and it can use a regular Linux/BSD server or Synology NAS as a host via SSH commands. That supports key-based login to self-hosted git servers. Automatic public-key registration is documented only for GitHub and BitBucket, and the evidence does not show how the public key is installed on your own servers or used beyond git, so the password-less server-access part is only partly covered. missing for 10: documented export or installation of the public key on arbitrary servers, supported key types/algorithms, evidence of password-less access beyond git hosting, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can generate SSH key pairs for password-less access to my servers

citations.quote: You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
If you tap "Connect with BitBucket" or "Connect with GitHub" your public key will automatically be registered with BitBucket or GitHub.
configure a regular Linux server, BSD server & Synology NAS to act as a hosting provider, using SSH commands for listing repositories.
